function.name: calculate_Bond_Price
function.description: Calculate the bond price based on its face value, coupon rate, required rate of return, and the number of years until maturity. The calculation assumes annual coupon payments. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

Face_Value.description: The nominal value or par value of the bond in dollars. This is a float type value.

Coupon_rate.description: The annual coupon rate of the bond expressed as a percentage (e.g., 5 for 5%). This is a float type value.

Required_return.description: The annual required rate of return for the bond investment expressed as a percentage (e.g., 5 for 5%). This is a float type value.

maturity_years.description: The number of whole years until the bond's maturity.

message.content:
I don’t have real‑time market data, so I can’t give you the exact spot price of gold for today.  As of the last published close (usually around 4 p.m. Eastern Time on the previous business day), U.S. spot gold was trading roughly **$1,950–$1,970 per troy ounce**.  

If you need the precise, up‑to‑minute price, you can check one of the following reliable sources:

| Source | How to access |
|--------|---------------|
| **Bloomberg** | `https://www.bloomberg.com/quote/GC=COM` |
| **Kitco** | `https://www.kitco.com/charts/livegold.html` |
| **London Metal Exchange (LME)** | `https://www.lme.com/en-GB/Metals/Gold` |
| **NYMEX (CME Group)** | `https://www.cmegroup.com/trading/metals/precious/spot-gold.html` |
| **Federal Reserve Economic Data (FRED)** | `https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/GOLDAMGBD228NLBM` (monthly average) |

These sites update the price every few seconds during market hours. If you’re looking for a historical trend or a specific date, most of them also provide charts and downloadable data.
